title: Graceful pagination fallback and lattice index coordinator
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Several dashboards show tail latency and elevated DB read amplification when clients request deep pagination (offsets > 10k) or when the materialized tenant-views are being rebuilt. Current cursor format is opaque and forces wide index scans or full-range merges on stale materialized segments, which spikes cost and p99 latency for a small subset of tenants.

Goal: Implement a server-side coordinator that (1) maintains a lightweight, shard-aware lattice index of available materialized segments and per-tenant bloom summaries, and (2) provides a graceful pagination fallback that automatically chooses a safe, low-cost query plan when the preferred fast-path is unavailable or would exceed latency/budget SLOs. The solution must be backward compatible with existing client cursors and controlled by a feature flag for staged rollout.

Design proposal:
- Lattice Index Coordinator (LIC): an in-memory, strongly-consistent (RAFT-backed) authority per region that tracks segment fragments, their compact fingerprints, and the last-updated timeline. LIC exposes a small read API used by query nodes to translate a client cursor into a fragment-aware plan. LIC stores bloom-filtered tenant prefixes to avoid scanning unrelated shards.
- Graceful pagination fallback: if LIC detects that preferred fragments are stale (rebuild in progress) or the predicted cost exceeds threshold, query node switches to a fallback plan: (a) bounded range scan using fragment anchors, (b) speculative micro-snapshot on hot fragment to serve first N pages while rebuild completes, or (c) truncated-page response with a lightweight hint for the client to re-issue with a short-lived strong cursor.
- Cursor compatibility: add a 1-byte version and optional fragment-id token to cursor payload. Old cursors remain valid; server interprets missing fragment-id as pre-lic path. All cursors still opaque to clients.
- Maintenance jobs: LIC refresh job runs every 3-5 minutes, heavy rebuilds scheduled with jitter and low-priority slots to avoid mass churn. A small windowed compaction will merge adjacent tiny fragments to reduce fragmentation noise.

Tradeoffs and rationale:
- Strong coordinator (LIC) introduces additional control-plane complexity and cross-node RPCs but reduces tail by avoiding blind wide scans. We accept modest memory/CP cost for coordinator to cut expensive backend reads.
- Micro-snapshots serve few pages quickly but may return slightly stale view; will be restricted to read-only dashboards with documented staleness bounds.

Implementation plan:
1) Spike (week 1): LIC prototype in Go, local memory-only, simulate fragment metadata and run synthetic bench against current query planner.
2) Server integration (week 2-3): light API for query nodes to consult LIC and a fallback planner in query node code path. Add feature flag gating.
3) Telemetry and safety nets (week 3): new metrics (predicted_cost, fallback_rate, fragment_staleness), dashboards, and an automated rollback when fallback_rate > 10% of queries for >5m.
4) Canary (week 4): region-limited rollout to non-critical tenants behind feature flag; compare p99/cost against control group.
5) Gradual ramp and postmortems (week 5-6).

Benchmarks: aim for >= 30% p99 reduction on deep pagination workloads and >= 25% fewer DB read bytes for affected tenants. Microbench harness in repo.

Links to artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CI/Lattice+Index+Coordinator (draft), GitHub spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/ pull/3441, bench dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/console/query-lic-bench

Notes: This ticket ties into ongoing work on materialized view rebuild coordination (dependency ENG-21104) and console query prefetching (dependency ENG-30482). Rollout must coordinate with SRE to ensure compaction jobs do not coincide with peak traffic windows.
acceptance_criteria: p99 tail latency for deep-pagination queries reduced by >= 30% in canary tenants compared to baseline
Fallback planner activates under predicted-cost guardrails and does not return errors to clients (0 customer-facing failures in canary)
Feature gated behind console.query.lic and rollout plan documented
Telemetry added: lic_query_calls, lic_fallback_count, fragment_rebuild_in_progress, predicted_cost_p90
Automated rollback alarm configured: fallback_rate > 10% sustained for 5m
